result.instructions:
Elmo tracks how AI models — ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews — mention and cite brands.

Start with list_brands to find a brand id; every other brand tool takes one.
get_analytics answers 'how is this brand doing'; get_citations and get_query_fanout answer 'why', and are where an
optimization plan comes from — the pages the models actually read and the searches they actually ran.

Analytics tools need a window: start and end as ISO 8601 timestamps, half-open, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.
Rates and shares are fractions of 1, not percentages.

Only the tools this connection is permitted appear in tools/list. Call whoami to see what it is and what it holds.

tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Identify this connection
tools.description: What this MCP connection is: who it acts as, which organizations it reaches, and which tools it may call. Needs no permission, so it is always safe to call first when a request fails and it is not clear why.

tools.name: list_models
tools.title: List models
tools.description: The models this deployment knows about, and which of them it is actually tracking. Use the returned ids for the `model` filter on any analytics tool.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.title: List brands
tools.description: Every brand this connection tracks. Start here: the other brand tools take an id from this list.

tools.name: get_brand
tools.title: Get one brand
tools.description: One brand's configuration: its domains, aliases, tracked models, and cadence.

tools.name: list_competitors
tools.title: List competitors
tools.description: The competitors tracked against a brand, with the domains and aliases a mention is matched on. These are what share of voice is measured against.

tools.name: get_billing
tools.title: Get plan and usage
tools.description: A workspace's plan, its limits, and how much of each is used. Read-only — there is no tool that changes a subscription.

organizationId.description: Organization id, from the organizationIds whoami reports.

tools.name: list_prompts
tools.title: List prompts
tools.description: The prompts asked of the models on a brand's behalf. `enabled` is what decides whether a prompt is still being sampled. This is the one list that can get long, so it pages.

brandId.description: Restrict to one brand. Omit for every brand in reach.

enabled.description: Restrict to prompts that are or aren't being sampled.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags; a prompt carrying any of them matches.

q.description: Substring match on the prompt text.

tools.name: list_prompt_tags
tools.title: List prompt tags
tools.description: The tags in use on a brand's prompts, with how many carry each. Tags are derived: one exists exactly as long as some prompt carries it.

tools.name: get_analytics
tools.title: Get a brand's analytics
tools.description: Everything a brand's window says in one call: visibility and its daily trend, share of voice against tracked competitors, the per-model breakdown, and citation totals. Also, experimentally: the sentiment of answers toward the brand and each competitor (positive, neutral, negative, mixed) and where each comes among the tracked companies an answer names (position 1 = named first), overall and per model, and per day for the brand. These count every answer in the window, while visibility and share of voice count each prompt's latest answers. The first thing to read when asked how a brand is doing. Rates are fractions of 1, not percentages.

start.description: Start of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Inclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

end.description: End of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Exclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

model.description: Restrict to one model, by id from list_models.

tags.description: Comma-separated prompt tags; only prompts carrying one are counted.

tools.name: get_prompt_performance
tools.title: Get per-prompt performance
tools.description: How each prompt performed over the window — which questions surface the brand and which don't, and (experimentally) how its answers describe the brand and where they place it among the tracked companies they name. Enabled prompts only; a disabled one isn't sampled, so it has nothing to report.

start.description: Start of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Inclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

end.description: End of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Exclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

model.description: Restrict to one model, by id from list_models.

tags.description: Comma-separated prompt tags; only prompts carrying one are counted.

tools.name: get_citations
tools.title: Get cited sources
tools.description: The pages the models cited while answering about this brand, by domain and by URL, each categorized as the brand's own, a competitor's, or editorial. The core of an AEO content plan: the editorial pages here are where the models are getting their answers. Returns the most cited domains and URLs; pass `search` to find a specific one anywhere in the window.

start.description: Start of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Inclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

end.description: End of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Exclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

model.description: Restrict to one model, by id from list_models.

tags.description: Comma-separated prompt tags; only prompts carrying one are counted.

search.description: Only rows containing this text, matched case-insensitively.

limit.description: Rows to return, most frequent first. Defaults to 50; the totals always cover every row.

tools.name: get_query_fanout
tools.title: Get the searches the models ran
tools.description: The web searches the models actually ran while answering, and how often. These are the phrasings to optimize for — they are frequently not the prompt's own wording. Returns the most run searches; pass `search` to find others.

start.description: Start of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Inclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

end.description: End of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Exclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

model.description: Restrict to one model, by id from list_models.

tags.description: Comma-separated prompt tags; only prompts carrying one are counted.

search.description: Only rows containing this text, matched case-insensitively.

limit.description: Rows to return, most frequent first. Defaults to 100; the totals always cover every row.

annotations.title: Get the searches the models ran

tools.name: get_opportunities
tools.title: Get the latest opportunities report
tools.description: The most recent stored opportunities report for a brand: what to write, what to fix, and the risks Elmo found. `status` says whether there was enough data to write one.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.title: List answers recorded for a prompt
tools.description: Metadata for the answers recorded for one prompt, newest first, including the mention judge's assessment, sentiment and position (experimental) for the brand and each competitor named. The answer text lives on get_run, which keeps this list small enough to page through.

start.description: Start of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Inclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

end.description: End of the window, an ISO 8601 timestamp with an offset. Exclusive, and aligned down to the quarter hour.

model.description: Restrict to one model, by id from list_models.

annotations.title: List answers recorded for a prompt

tools.name: get_run
tools.title: Get one answer in full
tools.description: One recorded answer: the model's reply as text, every page it cited, and for the brand and each competitor named, whether it counts as a mention, the sentiment toward it, and its position among the tracked companies named (experimental). Read this when you need to know *how* a model described the brand, not just whether it did.
